ideas.title: The scrap crane you play
ideas.critique: The last post came back up empty, so this is the step that makes it work: pegs as real contacting rigid bodies magnetised by a solved coil, played by the player, not filmed. The risk is another film of a coil that lifts nothing. If what it picks up doesn't really depend on how the pegs lie and the switch drop doesn't land on a friend live, it is the same post again.

ideas.title: Magnet drawing slate
ideas.critique: The ironsand needles have already been shown settling over a hidden stone. What is new is the player's hand moving the field live and friends guessing, which makes it a real toy. The guessing is the word game reskinned, and a single slate rig caps how real it is.

ideas.title: A cell in a clam shell
ideas.critique: A cell built from what touches what, with electrode potentials from a materials table, is core road work the island has never had. Played honestly, a clam cell barely warms a thin wire, so 'glows or does nothing' will mostly be 'nothing' unless numbers get fudged. That would cap it as a rig.

ideas.title: The copper gutter race
ideas.critique: Induced current is physics the island has never had, and the slow fall looks like magic. But image-dipole drag for one sheet geometry is a formula rig rather than a solver, and once the trick is known, betting on races wears thin quickly.

ideas.title: Fishing for iron off the pier
ideas.critique: It is a magnet-on-a-string treasure hunt, which is predictable. The stone picking up iron has been posted already, so the only new part is the pendulum and water drag. Real fishing play could carry it, but it is unlikely to surprise anyone.

ideas.title: A hot wire that carves wax
same_form: A copper wire keeps its bends
ideas.critique: A heated tool working a material, shown close up, is the island's craft-bench form again. Keeping the carved piece is a nice touch, but it depends on a cell strong enough to heat the wire, which the island doesn't have yet, so the power will likely be faked.

ideas.title: The galvanometer bowl
ideas.critique: This takes the compass bowl and gives it a real mechanism: a wound loop's field turning the needle. As a detector you take round and touch to everything, it gives players a reason to try things. Its value rests entirely on a cell model that doesn't exist yet; without one, the needle kicks on cue.

ideas.title: Iron bells on the friends
ideas.critique: This carries out the human's own example of friends reacting to a physics toy, and the tag game is a scripted chase with a bell sound added. At the stone's real range a bell would barely move, so the tug would have to be exaggerated.

ideas.title: The spinning coin motor
ideas.nearest: A wire that spins by itself
ideas.critique: The homopolar wire has already been posted as a film. Making it bendable and playable is a real step, but people who know the island have seen this exact motor spin. What's new depends on contact current and balance being solved rather than set by the bend.

ideas.title: Peg sculptures
ideas.critique: Branching iron trees that collapse when the switch opens would show soft iron magnetising iron at play rate, which is new. It overlaps heavily with the scrap crane and shares the same soft-iron-on-contact solve. If the chains are only 2 or 3 long, as softiron.jl gave in s148, there is no tree.
